# KM-135 — Web: agent attribution in the timeline

**Lane:** app · **Complexity:** 2 · **Model:** codex · **Depends on:** KM-104, KM-120, KM-122 · **Serializes with:** KM-130, KM-134, KM-172 (shared `matrix-browser.ts` and composition files)
**Plan context (pinned):** [M1 plan](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/plans/2026-10-01-002-refactor-external-m1-thin-path-plan.md) · [contracts](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/contracts.md) · [roster and graph](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/roster.md)
**Exclusive write surfaces:** `apps/web/src/features/timeline/{attribution.ts,attribution.test.ts,TimelineScreen.tsx,TimelineScreen.test.tsx}`. Additive edits in `apps/web/src/composition/human/{browser-api.ts,browser-api.test.ts,application.ts,room.tsx,matrix-browser.ts}` and `apps/web/src/main.tsx`.

## Outcome

- Agent messages render with author `Claude · Kevin` and the badge `Claude Code agent` (or `Codex agent`).
- A room member that the server reports as C3 `unknown` renders as `Unknown` and no longer makes the whole timeline unavailable.
- Human rows show the Matrix display name the server returns (C4: `ownerFirstName`, set by KM-122), and the viewer's own name follows the same rule.

## Context and evidence

- Plan U15, KTD9, R12. U15: "agent messages show as `Claude · Kevin` with an agent badge, using the owner map… An unknown sender renders as `Unknown`, with no crash. A human sender is unchanged."
- **Server shape after KM-122** (reconciliation A2; C3): there is no new route. The existing `POST /api/human/messaging/participants` keeps its request shape, and every response entry is a C3 `Participant`: today's keys plus a mandatory `kind`; agents add `ownerLabel` and `harness`; an unknown member is `{ matrixUserId, displayName, kind: 'unknown' }` and never fails the response. `displayName` is the member's Matrix display name (humans: `ownerFirstName`, set by KM-122 at session mint; agents: `Claude · Kevin`, set by KM-132 at registration), falling back to the user id.
- The browser's `ParticipantView` identity must keep Khala's `ownerId` and `participantId`, which C3 human and agent entries still carry:
  - `packages/messaging/src/channels/index.ts:63` throws unless `actor.ownerId === principal.ownerId`.
  - `channels/create.ts:23` checks the same thing.
  - `channels/send.ts:35` reconciles local echoes by `actor.participantId`.
- Today `browser-api.ts:345-372` (`participants.resolve`) requires each entry to have exactly the keys `matrixUserId, participantId, ownerId, displayName[, kind]` (`:354-356`) and returns `null` if any entry or user is missing. `matrix-browser.ts:574-577` then throws, and the whole timeline is unavailable. After KM-122, agent entries (extra `ownerLabel`/`harness`) and unknown entries (no `participantId`/`ownerId`) fail that exact-key check, so this ticket must update it.
- Row rendering: `apps/web/src/features/timeline/TimelineScreen.tsx:344-359` (author via `resolveDisplayName`, badge via `ownershipLabel(attributionFor(...))`). Helpers are in `apps/web/src/features/timeline/attribution.ts:21-45`.
- **Plan file corrections:**
  - U15 names `apps/web/src/ui/conversation/ChatMessage.tsx`, which does not exist. `ChatMessage` is in `apps/web/src/ui/conversation/ConversationLayout.tsx:54-70` and already renders `kindLabel` as a badge span (`:63`). That file is design-lane property (KM-182), so this ticket only passes `author`/`kindLabel` and **does not edit `ui/conversation/*`**.
  - U15 also names `composition/human/conversations.ts`, which is the conversation-index port and is unrelated; it is not touched.
- Own display name today is the full email: `matrix-browser.ts:342` and `:605` (`principal.verifiedEmail`). C4 assigns `ownerFirstName` to KM-135.

## Scope

1. In `browser-api.ts`, accept C3 entries in the existing `participants.resolve` POST decode (no new request, no GET).
2. Turn `kind: 'unknown'` entries into a synthesized `Unknown` view instead of failing.
3. Record C3 detail per `participantId` and expose `describe`.
4. Render the agent author and harness badge from that detail in `TimelineScreen`.
5. Show the viewer's own name as `ownerFirstName(email)`.

## Non-goals

- The server route and owner map → **KM-122**, **KM-132**. Any new participants route or GET call → none (A2).
- Header avatar stack and roster tree → **KM-183**. Bubble and badge visuals → **KM-182**. No CSS and no `ui/conversation/*` edits.
- Agent connection or heartbeat status (out of M1 per U15). Agent rename (deleted by **KM-120**).

## Contract and invariants

From contracts.md **C3** (verbatim):

> Participants: there is **no new route**. The existing `POST /api/human/messaging/participants` (`apps/control/src/composition/human/handlers.ts:31`, `:352-388` at `5db209cc`) keeps its request shape (`{ userIds, roomId?, deviceId?, matrixAccessToken?, targetParticipantIds? }`). Each entry of its `{ participants: [...] }` response keeps today's keys and gains `kind: 'human'|'agent'|'unknown'`, plus `ownerLabel` and `harness` when `kind === 'agent'`:

```ts
export type Participant =
  | { matrixUserId: string; participantId: string; ownerId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'human' }
  | { matrixUserId: string; participantId: string; ownerId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'agent'; ownerLabel: string; harness: Harness }
  | { matrixUserId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'unknown' };   // an unknown member never fails the whole response
export type ParticipantsResponse = { participants: Participant[] };
```

> - `displayName` is the member's Matrix display name (C4 human-label rule), falling back to `matrixUserId`.
> - KM-122 implements the augmentation; KM-135 consumes it through the existing caller in `apps/web/src/composition/human/browser-api.ts` (`MATRIX_PARTICIPANTS_PATH` `:53`, `participants.resolve` `:345-372`).

From **C4**: "Display name: `<label> · <ownerFirstName>`, for example `Claude · Kevin`." and "KM-122, KM-132 and KM-135 use this same rule via `ownerFirstName(email)` exported from `packages/contracts/src/m1/participants.ts`, which KM-104 owns." and "**Human labels come from Matrix display names, everywhere.**"

Imports:
- `Participant`, `decodeParticipant` and `ownerFirstName` from `@khala/contracts/m1/participants` (KM-104).
- `Harness` from `@khala/contracts/m1/agent-join`.

Do not re-declare any of these.

Invariants:
- Real Khala `ownerId`/`participantId` come only from C3 `human`/`agent` entries. Never synthesize them for humans or agents.
- An `Unknown` view is `{ participantId: \`unknown:${matrixUserId}\`, kind: 'human', ownerId: \`unknown:${matrixUserId}\`, displayName: 'Unknown', deviceIds: [] }`, passed through `decodeParticipantView`. Its `ownerId` can never equal a real owner.
- One POST per `resolve`, as today. No GET, no new path.

## Implementation pointers (refreshable @ 5db209cc)

### Files

- Modify:
  - `apps/web/src/composition/human/browser-api.ts`, `browser-api.test.ts`, `application.ts`, `room.tsx`, `matrix-browser.ts`
  - `apps/web/src/main.tsx`

### Worked example

`resolve(['@khala_m:hs', '@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:hs', '@stranger:hs'], _, '!r:hs', _, session)`:

1. `POST /api/human/messaging/participants` `{ userIds: [all three], roomId, deviceId, matrixAccessToken }` (unchanged request) →
   ```json
   { "participants": [
     { "matrixUserId": "@khala_m:hs", "participantId": "human_…", "ownerId": "owner_maya", "displayName": "Maya", "kind": "human" },
     { "matrixUserId": "@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:hs", "participantId": "agent_…", "ownerId": "owner_kevin", "displayName": "Claude · Kevin",
       "kind": "agent", "ownerLabel": "Kevin", "harness": "claude" },
     { "matrixUserId": "@stranger:hs", "displayName": "@stranger:hs", "kind": "unknown" } ] }
   ```
2. The result map holds 3 entries:
   - the human `{ participantId: 'human_…', kind: 'human', ownerId: 'owner_maya', displayName: 'Maya' }`;
   - the agent `{ participantId: 'agent_…', kind: 'agent', ownerId: 'owner_kevin', displayName: 'Claude · Kevin' }`;
   - the stranger `{ participantId: 'unknown:@stranger:hs', kind: 'human', ownerId: 'unknown:@stranger:hs', displayName: 'Unknown' }`.

   `describe('agent_…')` returns the C3 agent entry, and `describe('unknown:@stranger:hs')` returns the C3 unknown entry.

Rendered (viewer Kevin): agent row author `Claude · Kevin`, badge `Claude Code agent`; Maya `Maya` / `Human`; stranger `Unknown` (badge hidden because it equals the author); own rows `Kevin` / `You`.

### Steps

1. **browser-api.ts — decode.** Inside `participants.resolve`, keep the request (`:348`) and the envelope check (`:350-351`). Replace the per-entry exact-key check (`:354-356`) with `decodeParticipant(value)` (KM-104, C3). Then:
   - `human` or `agent` → `decodeParticipantView({ participantId, kind, ownerId, displayName, deviceIds: [] }, options.limits)` as today (`:357-363`).
   - `unknown` → the synthesized `Unknown` view (Invariants).
   - A decode failure or a duplicate `matrixUserId` → `null`, as today.
   - Record `details.set(view.participantId, entry)` for every entry, where `details` is a `Map<string, Participant>` held by the `participants` object.
   - Keep the completeness check at `:368-369` over the original `userIds` (unknown entries now satisfy it).
   - Add `describe(participantId: string): Participant | undefined` to `participants` and to the `HumanBrowserApi` type.
2. **application.ts.** Add `readonly describeParticipant?: (participantId: string) => Participant | undefined;` to `HumanApplicationPorts`.
3. **main.tsx.** Pass `describeParticipant: api.participants.describe` into `createHumanApplication`.
4. **attribution.ts.** Add
   ```ts
   export const HARNESS_NAMES: Readonly<Record<Harness, string>> = { claude: 'Claude Code', codex: 'Codex' };
   export function rowLabels(attribution: Attribution, detail: Participant | undefined): Readonly<{ author: string | null; kindLabel: string }>;
   ```
   - An agent detail returns `` { author: detail.displayName, kindLabel: `${HARNESS_NAMES[detail.harness]} agent` } ``.
   - An unknown detail returns `{ author: 'Unknown', kindLabel: 'Unknown' }`.
   - Anything else returns `{ author: null, kindLabel: ownershipLabel(attribution) }`.
5. **TimelineScreen.tsx.** Add the optional prop `describeParticipant?: (participantId: ParticipantId) => Participant | undefined`. In the row render (`:344-359`):
   - Compute `labels = rowLabels(attribution, describeParticipant?.(item.participant.participantId))`.
   - Set `author={labels.author ?? resolveDisplayName(…existing expression…)}` and `kindLabel={labels.kindLabel}`.
   - A detail-derived author is not replaced by "Agent name unavailable".
   - Do not change the markup structure.
6. **room.tsx.** Pass `{...(context.describeParticipant ? { describeParticipant: context.describeParticipant } : {})}` to `TimelineScreen`.
7. **matrix-browser.ts.** At `:342` and `:605`, replace `principal.verifiedEmail` with `ownerFirstName(principal.verifiedEmail)`.

## Test scenarios

`apps/web/src/composition/human/browser-api.test.ts`
1. Worked example: exactly one fetch (the POST; no GET). The result has 3 entries with the values above. `describe('agent_…').harness` is `'claude'`.
2. A response containing only `unknown` entries → the map holds only `Unknown` views; the result is not `null`.
3. An agent entry missing `ownerLabel`, or a human entry with an extra `harness` → `null`.
4. Update the legacy decode test at `:338-360` to C3 entries (`kind` present); with no `roomId` it still sends the same body.

`apps/web/src/features/timeline/attribution.test.ts` (new)
5. `rowLabels`:
   - Agent detail (`displayName: 'Codex · Maya'`, harness `codex`) → `{ author: 'Codex · Maya', kindLabel: 'Codex agent' }`.
   - Unknown detail → `Unknown` / `Unknown`.
   - Human detail → `{ author: null, kindLabel: 'Human' }`.
   - No detail and viewer-owned → `{ author: null, kindLabel: 'You' }`.

`apps/web/src/features/timeline/TimelineScreen.test.tsx`
6. An agent row with a C3 detail renders `Claude · Kevin` and `Claude Code agent`, and neither "Your agent" nor "Another person's agent".
7. An `Unknown` sender row renders `Unknown` without throwing.
8. A human-only timeline renders identical markup with and without `describeParticipant`.
9. With `namesReady: false`, a C3 agent row still shows `Claude · Kevin`.

Done when the scenarios pass and `grep -n "messaging/participants?roomId" -r apps/web/src` prints nothing. In the KM-150/KM-151 runs, both humans see agent rows as `<label> · <owner>` with the harness badge, and human rows show first names.

## Risks and stop conditions

- **Stop** if KM-122 merged a response shape that differs from C3 as quoted, or added a GET route.
- **Stop** if KM-104's `participants.ts` lacks `decodeParticipant` or `ownerFirstName`, or its shapes differ from C3/C4 as quoted.
- **Ordering:** this ticket edits `main.tsx`, `application.ts`, `room.tsx` and `matrix-browser.ts`, which KM-120 rewrites (a dependency).
- Do not edit `apps/web/src/ui/conversation/*`, even if the badge looks plain. Note it for KM-182. Earlier drafts listed KM-182 as `serializes_with`; roster v2 does not, because this ticket does not edit design-lane files.

## Complexity rationale

2: about 110 lines across one adapter, one pure label function and one render site, plus tests. The care is in keeping real identity intact (the channel service requires the real `ownerId`) and in never letting one unknown member null the timeline.
